title: Duration Gap and Interest-Sensitive Gap

maps.tested: Five sources, including a reported count of two questions in one sitting. Tested as a directional impact question on net worth rather than as pure arithmetic.
maps.specifics: Reported: 'duration gap'; 'impact of asset and liability values on net worth given duration of asset and liability'; 'duration of asset liability (2)'; 'IS gap' and 'ISR gap LR'. Closed-book: change in NW = -[D_A x A - D_L x L] x change in r / (1 + r). The polarity of the leveraged-adjusted duration gap against a rate move is the single most corruptible fact here.

vardeezReading: LTR-17: Very Important. "Entire Chapter and Each Learning Objective is Important - so Do not Ignore this Chapter".

selectors.name: Duration gap, plain form
selectors.what: Leverage-adjusted duration gap DGAP = D_A - D_L x (L/A) from the asset and liability durations and the balance sheet amounts, in the plain form of the August recall.
selectors.theory: Why liabilities are scaled by L/A (assets exceed liabilities, so liability values must move by slightly more than asset values to immunise), and what the gap measures: the mismatch of rate sensitivity between assets and liabilities.

selectors.name: Net worth impact from durations, with direction
selectors.what: Change in net worth for a given rate move: change in NW = -D_A x A x di/(1+i) + D_L x L x di/(1+i) = -DGAP x A x di/(1+i), with the direction (gain or loss) stated.
selectors.theory: Net worth changes with the size of the duration gap, the size of the institution and the size of the rate change; the rate change is divided by one plus the original rate.

selectors.name: Liability duration that immunises net worth
selectors.what: Reverse-solve of DGAP = 0: D_L = D_A x A/L, the liability duration (or the asset duration or the A to L balance) that leaves net worth unchanged for a rate move.
selectors.theory: Zero leverage-adjusted gap immunises net worth; the gap can be closed by changing D_A, D_L or the relative amounts of A and L.

selectors.name: IS gap, ISR and change in NII
selectors.what: ISGAP = ISA - ISL, relative ISGAP = ISGAP / size of institution, ISR = ISA / ISL; cumulative gap over the planning horizon and the change in net interest income: change in NII = change in i x cumulative gap.
selectors.theory: Asset sensitive (positive ISGAP, ISR above 1) gains NII when rates rise; liability sensitive (negative ISGAP, ISR below 1) loses NII when rates rise; the horizon matters and the cumulative gap, not one bucket, drives the change in NII.

selectors.name: Trap: polarity of the leverage-adjusted gap
selectors.what: The sign of DGAP after the leverage adjustment against a rate move: positive gap loses net worth when rates rise and gains when they fall, negative gap the reverse; D_A below D_L can still give a positive DGAP when L/A is low enough.

notSelected: LTR-17 a (asset-liability management strategies in general: asset, liability and funds management, the ALCO, price and reinvestment risk) and LTR-17 d (limitations of ISGAP and duration gap management) carry no shape, no Map point and no Vardeez pointer, and the weighted gap and basis risk, NIM itself and the aggressive versus defensive strategies are likewise not selected.
